# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A 4-day Kyoto base trip works best with one hotel for all nights, temple-focused days, one light hiking day, and food stops clustered by neighborhood to keep transit low.
Budget target: **USD 1,800 total excluding flights** for 2 adults, with a comfortable mid-range pace.

## 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget

| Day | Focus | Morning | Afternoon | Dinner | Est. Local Transport |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mar 18 | Higashiyama temples | Kiyomizu-dera; Sannenzaka stroll | Kodai-ji; Yasaka Shrine; Maruyama Park | Gion kaiseki or yudofu | **JPY 1,200** |
| Mar 19 | Arashiyama nature + light hike | Bamboo Grove; Tenryu-ji | Iwatayama Monkey Park; Togetsukyo Bridge | Arashiyama soba or tofu set | **JPY 1,400** |
| Mar 20 | Fushimi + food lanes | Fushimi Inari Taisha early visit | Fushimi sake district; Nishiki Market | Pontocho izakaya | **JPY 1,600** |
| Mar 21 | Northern temples + flexible wrap-up | Kinkaku-ji; Ryoan-ji | Daitoku-ji or Philosopher’s Path if energy allows | Kyoto station area dinner | **JPY 1,300** |

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Plan

### Day 1: Higashiyama Temple Circuit
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Start at **Kiyomizu-dera** early to avoid crowds; walk downhill through **Sannenzaka** and **Ninenzaka**.
- Afternoon: Visit **Kodai-ji** and **Yasaka Shrine**, then relax at **Maruyama Park**.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f8/A199_Japan_Kyoto_Maruyama_Park_Gion_Ar%C3%A9a_%284764445344%29.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Visit **Kodai-ji** and **Yasaka Shrine**, then relax at **Maruyama Park**, Kyoto, Japan
- Food: Try **yuba**, **matcha sweets**, and a simple **tofu set meal** in Gion.
- Transport: Mostly walking plus short bus/taxi hops; budget **JPY 1,200**.

### Day 2: Arashiyama and Light Hiking
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** and **Tenryu-ji**.
- Afternoon: Do the light hike up **Iwatayama Monkey Park** for city views, then cross **Togetsukyo Bridge**.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: Do the light hike up **Iwatayama Monkey Park** for city views, then cross **Togetsukyo Bridge**, Kyoto, Japan
- Food: Eat **soba**, **tofu dengaku**, or a riverside lunch near Arashiyama Station.
- Transport: Train + local bus + short taxi if needed; budget **JPY 1,400**.

### Day 3: Fushimi Inari and Local Food
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** at opening time for quieter torii paths.
- Afternoon: Explore the **Fushimi sake district** or head to **Nishiki Market** for tastings and souvenir snacks.
Media: Alt=Afternoon: Explore the **Fushimi sake district** or head to **Nishiki Market** for tastings and souvenir snacks, Kyoto, Japan
- Food: Focus on **yakitori**, **pickles**, **tamago-yaki**, and **sake tasting** if desired.
- Transport: JR/train plus subway or bus; budget **JPY 1,600**.

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto and Easy Finish
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Visit **Kinkaku-ji** first, then continue to **Ryoan-ji**.
- Afternoon: If you want more walking, choose **Daitoku-ji** or a gentle **Philosopher’s Path** stroll.
- Food: End with a Kyoto-style dinner near **Kyoto Station** for easy departure logistics.
- Transport: Bus + train mix; budget **JPY 1,300**.

## Budget Breakdown for 2 Adults

| Category | Estimated Cost |
|---|---:|
| Hotel, 3 nights, 1 room | **USD 450–750** |
| Local transport | **USD 35–50** |
| Food and drinks | **USD 280–420** |
| Temple/admission fees | **USD 40–80** |
| Snacks, tea, small purchases | **USD 60–120** |
| Buffer for taxi/rain/extra meal | **USD 100–150** |
| Total estimated trip spend | **USD 965–1,570** |

Best fit for your budget: a **mid-range hotel around Kyoto Station, Gion, or Karasuma** keeps transit simple and usually leaves room for nicer meals or one taxi day.

## Packing Checklist for Early Spring in Kyoto

- Light waterproof jacket or compact rain shell
- Warm layer: sweater, fleece, or light down jacket
- Long-sleeve tops and comfortable pants
- Walking shoes with good grip
- Socks you can wear all day; extra pair for rainy days
- Small umbrella
- Portable power bank
- Reusable water bottle
- Cash and IC card wallet
- Tissue pack and hand sanitizer
- Optional: scarf and thin gloves for cool mornings
